top_concerns: Gains over MATES (0.2-0.6 avg points; 1.4 at 2.8B) are within reported standard errors and round-1 run-to-run variation; single runs, no seeds or significance tests
1.7x speedup claim is read from single-run curves with tiny separation, against one baseline, at 1B only
Headline tables compare only Random and MATES; MATES also trains from scratch, so the 'no external model' framing is weak and the long-term-influence benefit is not isolated by ablation
Number inconsistencies (1B BLISS FLOPs 8.08 vs 19.53, 2.5B vs 2.8B, Table 2 round-1 mismatch, Table 5 per-task values) and an approximate softmax/hypergradient with no analysis
Validation sets (LAMBADA/ARC-E/PIQA) overlap with evaluation tasks; limited scale and corpora; compute advantage holds only at 1B
